new.title: Wander the rock-cut churches of Göreme Open-Air Museum
new.desc: A UNESCO-listed monastic complex of rock-cut churches, chapels and refectories, with 10th to 13th century frescoes. The Dark Church (Karanlık Kilise) keeps the best-preserved colours thanks to its tiny windows.
new.tip: Arrive at opening to beat the tour groups; the Dark Church needs a separate ticket. Allow about two hours.
new.q: Göreme Açık Hava Müzesi, Göreme, Nevşehir

new.title: See the frescoes of Tokalı Church
new.desc: Tokalı Kilise is the largest rock-cut church of the Göreme valley, with a barrel-vaulted old church and a newer nave painted in vivid blue and red. It stands just below the open-air museum complex.
new.tip: Check whether it is covered by the Open-Air Museum ticket; visit early or late in the day.
new.q: Tokalı Kilise, Göreme Açık Hava Müzesi, Göreme, Nevşehir

new.title: Climb Uçhisar Castle for the highest view in Cappadocia
new.desc: A huge volcanic rock pierced by tunnels and rooms, the highest point of the region. From the top the view runs from Göreme and Pigeon Valley to Mount Erciyes.
new.tip: Go at sunset when the light turns the valleys orange; there is an entrance fee and steep stairs.

new.title: Explore the rock fortress of Ortahisar
new.desc: Ortahisar Castle is a large natural rock used as a fortress and later as a food store, since the cool interior kept lemons and potatoes fresh. A stairway leads to a rooftop viewpoint over the village.
new.tip: Less crowded than Uçhisar; combine with the Rose Valley viewpoint nearby.

new.title: Visit the cave church of Çavuşin
new.desc: Çavuşin Church (Church of St John the Baptist) is an early rock church with frescoes in a cliff above the old abandoned village. The old village of cave houses lies beside it.
new.tip: Short climb from the main road; walk through the abandoned village for sunset views.

new.title: Walk among the mushroom chimneys of Paşabağ
new.desc: Paşabağ (Monks Valley) has the region's best triple-capped fairy chimneys and was used by hermit monks for seclusion. The site is a short walk from the road.
new.tip: Ticket is shared with Zelve; early morning or sunset gives the best light.
new.q: Paşabağ Müzesi, Zelve Yolu, Çavuşin, Avanos, Nevşehir

new.title: Explore the abandoned cave village of Zelve
new.desc: Zelve is a valley of abandoned cave dwellings, churches and a rock mill, inhabited until the 1950s when erosion forced the move to Yeni Zelve. It is a short drive from Avanos.
new.tip: Some churches are closed; bring good shoes. The ticket is shared with Paşabağ.
new.q: Zelve Açık Hava Müzesi, Zelve, Avanos, Nevşehir

new.title: Spot animal shapes in Devrent (Imagination) Valley
new.desc: Devrent Valley is full of tall cone-shaped chimneys that people say resemble camels and other animals, the best known being the Camel rock. It can be seen from a roadside parking area.
new.tip: Free and uncrowded; it fits well between Paşabağ and Avanos.

new.title: Make a wish on Temenni Hill above Ürgüp
new.desc: Temenni Hill (Wishing Hill) is the highest point in Ürgüp and has a panorama over the town and, on clear days, towards Mount Erciyes. Rock tombs and a small museum house are on the slopes.
new.tip: Easy walk from the main square; visit at sunset.

new.title: Descend into the Güray Ceramic Museum in Avanos
new.desc: A museum carved beneath the rocks of Avanos, displaying ceramics from different periods of Cappadocia's pottery tradition. It belongs to the Güray family workshop.
new.tip: Combine with a pottery demonstration.

new.title: Look over the rock chimneys of Love Valley
new.desc: Love Valley (Aşıklar Vadisi) is a short valley of tall phallus-shaped tuff chimneys between Göreme and Çavuşin. Its viewpoint can be reached by car or on foot.
new.tip: Walk it from Göreme for free; bring water and sturdy shoes.

new.title: Watch the sun go down at Göreme Sunset Point
new.desc: A hilltop terrace above Göreme town facing the valleys and fairy chimneys. It is the nearest viewpoint to the village and is busy at dusk.
new.tip: Arrive 45 minutes before sunset; free to enter.
new.q: Göreme Sunset View Point, Göreme, Nevşehir

new.title: Eat testi kebabı at Dibek in Göreme
new.desc: Dibek is a restored stone house in central Göreme known for traditional Cappadocian dishes, notably testi kebabı, meat and vegetables sealed in a clay pot and broken open at the table.
new.tip: Ask for the testi kebabı in advance, as it takes time to cook.

new.title: Try clay-pot kebab at Seten Anatolian Cuisine
new.desc: Seten opened in 2010 around an arched courtyard and serves Anatolian dishes, with a signature pottery kebab prepared on the spot. It is a more polished option in Göreme.
new.tip: Book a table on the terrace for sunset views.

new.title: Dine in an old cave stable at Topdeck Cave Restaurant
new.desc: Topdeck Cave Restaurant occupies a restored cave stable in Göreme and is among its most consistently rated restaurants. Pottery kebab and lamb dishes are on the menu.
new.tip: Book ahead in high season; try the pottery kebab.

new.title: Taste the kebab at Pumpkin Göreme
new.desc: Pumpkin Göreme is known for its lanterns made from colourful gourds and for affordable kebabs. It is a casual place in the old centre of Göreme.
new.tip: Visit in the evening when the lanterns are lit.

new.title: Order the lamb kebab at Sedef Restaurant
new.desc: Sedef is a Göreme restaurant serving a Turkish and international menu, with a signature lamb kebab.
new.tip: Reserve on busy nights.

new.title: Eat apple börek at Nazar Börek
new.desc: Nazar Börek in Göreme serves savoury and sweet böreks, with its elma böreği (apple pastry) singled out by guides. It is a quick breakfast or lunch stop.
new.tip: Go before noon; prices are low.

new.title: Eat home cooking at Zeytin Café in Ürgüp
new.desc: Zeytin Café & Ev Yemekleri is a small Ürgüp restaurant cited by Culinary Backstreets for a local-favourite testi kebabı, alongside clay-pot beans and mantı.
new.tip: Ask whether the testi kebabı needs pre-ordering.
new.q: Zeytin Cafe & Ev Yemekleri, Atatürk Bulvarı No:31, İmran Mahallesi, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Break open a pottery kebab at Dimrit Restaurant
new.desc: Dimrit is an Ürgüp restaurant in the town centre known for its pottery kebab and Anatolian dishes.
new.tip: Book ahead for the pottery kebab.

new.title: Dine under Temenni Hill at Ehlikeyf
new.desc: Ehlikeyf stands on the west end of Atatürk Bulvarı in Ürgüp, its dining room overlooking Wishing Hill, with live music most evenings from 20:30.
new.tip: Try the Cappadocian specialities and local wine.
new.q: Ehlikeyf Restaurant, Atatürk Bulvarı, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Eat well-priced Turkish dishes at Sofra in Ürgüp
new.desc: Sofra is on Atatürk Bulvarı near the main square and is praised by Wikivoyage for cooking that is good value for money. Sit indoors, as the street is busy.
new.tip: Choose the daily stews and kebabs.
new.q: Sofra Restaurant, Atatürk Bulvarı, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Have lunch in the stone house of Bizim Ev
new.desc: Bizim Ev is a restored old stone house in Avanos serving reliable Turkish dishes at fair prices, popular with groups. It is tucked away from the main road.
new.tip: Try the pottery kebab or a lamb stew.

new.title: Eat kebabs at Dayının Yeri in Avanos
new.desc: Dayının Yeri is a kebab restaurant near the bridge on the road from Göreme to Avanos, highly regarded for its grilled meats.
new.tip: Pair it with a pottery stop in the afternoon.

new.title: Eat testi kebabı at House of Memories in Uçhisar
new.desc: House of Memories is a restaurant in Uçhisar that Turkish bloggers rate among the best places for testi kebabı in Cappadocia.
new.tip: Reserve and order the pot kebab early.
new.q: House of Memories Restaurant, Uçhisar, Nevşehir

new.title: Have sunset drinks on Lil'a's terrace in Uçhisar
new.desc: Lil'a, part of the Museum Hotel, has a terrace that overlooks Uçhisar, with a view that is especially good at sunset. It serves contemporary Turkish dishes.
new.tip: Book for sunset; prices are high.
new.q: Lil'a Restaurant, Museum Hotel, Tekelli Mahallesi No:1, Uçhisar, Nevşehir

new.title: Taste local dishes with a view at Seki Restaurant
new.desc: Seki Restaurant in Uçhisar serves local Cappadocian cuisine with a wide view of the valleys.
new.tip: Try it at lunch for the view.

new.title: Dine beneath the fortress at Millocal
new.desc: Millocal is a newer restaurant-bar in Uçhisar sitting just under the castle, listed among the viewpoint restaurants of Cappadocia.
new.tip: Go at dusk for views of the lit castle.

new.title: Fly with Royal Balloon over the valleys
new.desc: Royal Balloon has operated in Cappadocia since 2010, with a maximum of 20 passengers per flight and breakfast served at its Göreme base. Flights lift off at dawn over the Göreme valleys.
new.tip: Book weeks ahead; flights depend on wind and can be cancelled.
new.q: Royal Balloon, Avcılar Mahallesi, Göreme, Nevşehir

new.title: Float at dawn with Butterfly Balloons
new.desc: Butterfly Balloons is a Göreme operator whose pilots hold commercial licences and which is part owned by the owner of the Kelebek Hotel.
new.tip: Book months ahead for summer.

new.title: Take off with Kapadokya Balloons
new.desc: Kapadokya Balloons is described as the oldest and largest balloon company in Cappadocia, flying since 1991 from Göreme.
new.tip: Dawn departures; hotel transfer is usual.

new.title: Throw a pot at Chez Galip pottery and hair museum
new.desc: Chez Galip is the best-known pottery workshop in Avanos, working red clay from the Kızılırmak river. Its cave-like cellar holds the hair museum with locks from thousands of women.
new.tip: Join a short wheel-throwing session; open 10:00 to 20:00.
new.q: Chez Galip Saç Müzesi, Kızılırmak Caddesi 401. Sokak No:91, Yeni Mahalle, Avanos, Nevşehir

new.title: Watch red clay turned at Kaya Seramik
new.desc: Kaya Seramik House is a pottery workshop and shop near Avanos, making ceramics from the red clay of the Kızılırmak.
new.tip: Ask for a demonstration or a wheel lesson.

new.title: Stroll the Kızılırmak riverside in Avanos
new.desc: The Kızılırmak (Red River), Turkey's longest, runs through Avanos and its red clay feeds the town's pottery industry. A riverside walk crosses the bridge to the potters' quarter.
new.tip: Best in the late afternoon.

new.title: Taste Cappadocian wines at Turasan Winery
new.desc: Turasan has a shop and tasting bar at its bottling facility on Tevfik Fikret Caddesi in Ürgüp and offers tasting tours of vineyard and cellar.
new.tip: Open daily; book a tour with four tastings.
new.q: Turasan Şarapçılık, Tevfik Fikret Caddesi, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Sip Cappadocian wine at Kocabağ Winery
new.desc: Kocabağ is a pioneer of commercial Cappadocian wine, with tastings and vineyard visits near Ürgüp and Uçhisar.
new.tip: Check which tasting room is open before you go.
new.q: Kocabağ Şarap Evi, Tevfik Fikret Caddesi, Ürgüp, Nevşehir

new.title: Hike Pigeon Valley from Uçhisar to Göreme
new.desc: A trail follows Güvercinlik Valley between Uçhisar and Göreme, past rock dovecotes cut in the cliffs. It takes about two hours.
new.tip: Start at the Uçhisar viewpoint and finish in Göreme; carry water.

new.title: Hike Rose Valley to the panoramic viewpoint
new.desc: The Güllüdere trails link the Panoramic Viewpoint near Ortahisar with Çavuşin, through rose-coloured rock. The hike is best at sunset.
new.tip: Allow 2 to 3 hours; wear solid shoes.

new.title: Catch sunset over Red Valley (Kızılçukur)
new.desc: Red Valley, near Çavuşin and Ortahisar, glows crimson as the sun sets. A viewpoint above the ravine is a standard sunset stop.
new.tip: Arrive early; free.

new.title: Ride at Katpatuka Horses Ranch in Çavuşin
new.desc: A family-run horse ranch in Çavuşin that leads rides through the surrounding valleys. Sunset and morning rides are available.
new.tip: Book ahead and say how experienced you are so they match the horse.
new.q: Katpatuka Horses Ranch, Çavuşin, Avanos, Nevşehir
